subject: sociology
title: Stratification & Differentiation: Class
welcome_lead: Marx and Weber lay foundations for thinking about class.
meta_desc: A-Level Sociology stratification class Marx Weber bourgeoisie status.
final_note: Class is both economy (Marx) and life chances (Weber).

concepts.def: Marx — owners of means of production.
Marx prediction — society splits into two classes.
Weber — social prestige distinct from economic class.
Weber — power to achieve political goals.

walkthroughs.body_html: Marx (1867) saw class as economic: bourgeoisie own production, proletariat sell labour. Surplus value extracted from workers. Marx predicted class polarisation, class consciousness and revolution. Modern critics note middle class grew rather than shrank.

Weber (1922) added status (social prestige, e.g. clergy) and party (political power) to class. Class is about market position; status about lifestyle. Weber identified four classes: propertied, professional, petty bourgeois, working — more nuanced than Marx's binary.

Modern measures use occupation: UK NS-SEC has 8 classes. Goldthorpe: middle-class jobs grew, working-class shrank. Savage et al. (2013) Great British Class Survey identified 7 classes including elite, precariat, and emergent service workers — combining economic, social and cultural capital.
